overview: A line-following robot needs to know exactly where a dark line sits relative to its body, not just whether one is present — which is why these sensors are almost always sold as a bar of several TCRT5000 reflectance sensors side by side (commonly 5) rather than a single unit. Each channel works like a miniature IR obstacle sensor: an emitter shines IR down at the floor, a receiver measures how much bounces back, and a comparator turns that into a digital HIGH/LOW for 'line' vs 'no line' at that specific position. Reading all channels together tells the robot not just that it's found the line, but which direction it needs to steer to stay centered on it.
simpleSummary: A row of sensors that see a dark line on the floor, so a robot can follow it.

specifications.outputType: Digital per channel (some versions also expose analog per-channel output)

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input for all sensor channels.

pinMap.name: OUT1
pinMap.function: Digital output for the leftmost sensor channel.
pinMap.gotcha: Must be held very close to the surface (a few mm) — mounting height that works on one floor surface may need retuning on another.

pinMap.name: OUT3
pinMap.function: Digital output for the center sensor channel.

pinMap.name: OUT5
pinMap.function: Digital output for the rightmost sensor channel.

useCases.title: Line-following robot
useCases.scenario: Read all channels to determine steering correction — e.g. if the rightmost sensor sees the line, steer right.

useCases.title: Maze-solving robot
useCases.scenario: Combine line detection with junction/intersection detection for maze navigation algorithms.

oftenConfusedWith: Single-channel IR obstacle sensor (presence detection only, not line position)
oftenUpgradedTo: Camera-based line following (more robust to lighting/surface variation)
